tasks.title: Fold MovementSystem.EngageDir into SimWorld.Hash's chain
tasks.why: Engage.cs:226 hashes movement.Engage and stops; MeleeSystem.cs:202,204 write EngageDir and its Hash (409-419) skips it; MovementSystem.cs:489 hashes only LeapTicks/LeapTarget. EngageDir steers a man (MovementSystem.cs:277), his step-in (274) and his yaw (456), with no SimHash call on it anywhere in Assets. A split there surfaces a tick later, blamed on Position/Yaw instead of its real cause.
tasks.done_when: SimHashTests covers EngageDir in the chain, and DeterminismReplayTests is green after the ReplayRecorder.FormatVersion bump

tasks.title: Use MapData.PropsByCell in VehicleKinematics instead of walking all Props
tasks.why: VehicleKinematics.cs:352 (FellUnder, once per moving machine per tick), VehicleKinematics.cs:314 (blocked-cell tree search) and VehicleKinematics.Wrecks.cs:35 (GrindWrecks, every 10th tick) each scan all of map.Props linearly, though MapData.cs:68-70 built PropsByCell exactly so a query asks for nearby props instead of walking them all; only Deformation.cs:156 reads it today.
tasks.done_when: a PropIndexTests-style test counts prop touches for one machine on a map with many props and shows the count drop, with TankMobilityTests and WreckDecayTests unchanged

tasks.title: FlowFieldManager.MarkCostDirty(navCell) ignores navCell, marks every goal
tasks.why: FlowFieldManager.cs:140-144 never reads its navCell argument and all three callers (VehicleKinematics.cs:329, Deformation.cs:147, DirectFire.Wrecks.cs:75) pass literal 0, so every nav change marks all up-to-32 goals dirty and Step pays two full-grid Dijkstras a tick for as long as anything keeps changing. The 'A4 may narrow this' comment names no caller that could narrow it.
tasks.done_when: FlowFieldManagerTests extended with a goal left clean when a far-off cell changes

tasks.title: Merge the duplicated 'at his post' 0.9m rule in SeparationJob and MovementSystem
tasks.why: SeparationJob.cs:33,46-56 (PostNear = 0.9f, OnTheWay) and MovementSystem.cs:313-314 (atPost, the same 0.9 as a bare literal) are two copies of one rule and number, and they differ: OnTheWay zeroes y and skips the ladder-post case atPost handles.
tasks.done_when: TrenchSpreadTests and GarrisonAndOrdersTests stay green after the two copies become one
